stem: About three-fourths of world's cobalt, a metal required for the manufacture of batteries for electric motor vehicles, is produced by

options.c: the Democratic Republic of the Congo

ex.summary: The DR Congo supplies roughly three-quarters of the world's mined cobalt, mostly from the copper-cobalt belt in its south-east. Argentina is known for lithium, Kazakhstan for uranium.

hook: Who mines ¾ of the world's cobalt?

aarav.line: EV batteries? Lithium Triangle. Argentina, obviously.

priya.line: Wait. Lithium isn't cobalt. I'd say Congo.

answer_head: DR Congo: about ¾ of world cobalt.

points.p: DR Congo paused cobalt exports to curb oversupply.
Ban replaced by quotas, up to 96,600 t a year in 2026–27.

trap: “EV battery” made Aarav think lithium. Argentina mines lithium, not cobalt.
method: Tag each option with its signature mineral. Wrong mineral? Cut it.
